meta.name: Frontend Product Builder Layout Components
meta.description: Canonical shared layout components that implement application shells, page structure, hierarchy, spacing ownership, responsive transformation, and content regions.

AppShell.name: AppShell
AppShell.description: Canonical authenticated application frame containing persistent navigation, global header, route content, and global feedback infrastructure.
capabilities: Compose persistent application navigation and route content.
Define the primary application scroll owner.
Transform navigation between sidebar, rail, and drawer patterns.
Host global feedback portals and session-level overlays.

foundation.reason: The product requires explicit scroll, navigation, context, and responsive-shell ownership beyond a generic primitive.

prohibitedUse: Focused full-screen workflow that explicitly replaces the shell.

slots.name: navigation
slots.description: Persistent or off-canvas primary product navigation.
contentRestrictions: Navigation must use user-oriented product grouping.
Feature-specific forms are prohibited.

slots.name: header
contentRestrictions: Page-specific primary actions normally remain outside the global header.

slots.name: content
contentRestrictions: Only one main landmark may be active.

slots.name: feedback
slots.description: Global portals, toasts, command menus, and session dialogs.
contentRestrictions: Local field errors do not belong here.

props.name: navigationMode
props.description: Resolved navigation presentation selected by responsive application behavior.
restrictions: Screens must not set this independently.

spacingOwnership: AppShell owns spacing and dimensions between navigation, global header, and content canvas.
Route recipes own spacing inside the content canvas.
composition.surfaceOwnership: AppShell owns the application canvas and persistent shell surfaces.
rules: Use one AppShell per authenticated application root.
Use one primary vertical route-content scroll owner.
Tenant or organization changes must not leave previous-context content visible.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Canonical implementation of the application-shell recipe.
Authentication uses a focused standalone layout.

prohibited: Direct token access in presentation components.

notes: Application infrastructure owns navigation presentation and global context.
Route state remains outside the shell.
Navigation and skip-link focus are owned by shell infrastructure.
Organization switching is delegated to application context.

responsive.strategy: Transform persistent navigation from sidebar to rail to drawer while preserving one route-content canvas.
responsive.compact: Off-canvas navigation drawer, compact global header, single route-content column.
responsive.medium: Compact navigation rail and flexible route-content canvas.
responsive.wide: Persistent labeled sidebar and flexible route-content canvas.
responsive.ultrawide: Persistent constrained sidebar; route recipes determine content width.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Navigation may scroll vertically; route content must not cause shell-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Shell must remain navigable at 200% text scaling and 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: application layout containing labeled nav, header, and one main landmark
accessibility.accessibleName: Primary navigation and utility regions use explicit labels.
keyboard: Provide a skip link to route content.
Compact drawer traps and restores focus.
focus: Focus order follows navigation, global utilities, and route content.
announcements: Route changes update document title and orientation.
Session and organization-context changes are perceivable.
aria: Do not create duplicate unlabeled navigation landmarks.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Active navigation and organization context do not depend only on color.

content.minimum: Navigation, global header, and one active route.
content.typical: Grouped navigation, organization context, utilities, route content, and feedback portals.
content.maximum: Several grouped product areas without rendering every route simultaneously.
content.wrapping: Navigation labels support localization according to the navigation component contract.
content.truncation: Organization names may truncate only when full value remains accessible.
content.localization: Shell controls must support expanded labels without consuming excessive route width.
content.emptyBehavior: A shell without an active route renders a safe route fallback.
content.technicalContent: Raw tenant IDs, tokens, route implementation details, and backend module names are prohibited.

PageContainer.name: PageContainer
PageContainer.description: Canonical route-level container that applies approved horizontal padding, maximum width, centering, and full-bleed behavior.
capabilities: Apply consistent route horizontal padding.
Select constrained, fluid, hybrid, or full-bleed page width.
Keep content aligned across route regions.
Prevent arbitrary page-level width decisions.

foundation.reason: Page-width and padding ownership must remain centralized and semantic.

constrained.intent: Constrain reading, authentication, or form content.

fluid.intent: Use available route width for tables, dashboards, and workspaces.
prohibitedUse: Long textual reading without inner constraint.

hybrid.intent: Combine fluid route width with constrained inner regions.

fullBleed.intent: Allow approved content to reach the content-canvas edges.

slots.name: content
contentRestrictions: Nested PageContainer usage requires an explicit layout reason.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Select according to the layout recipe.

spacingOwnership: The selected recipe owns vertical spacing between major regions.
composition.surfaceOwnership: PageContainer does not own a visual card surface.
rules: Use one primary PageContainer per route.
Do not wrap every section in another width container.
Inner reading or form constraints use approved nested layout components.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use fluid dashboard width.
Use fluid data width.
Use hybrid width.
Use constrained form width.

responsive.strategy: Adjust horizontal padding and width constraints according to the approved design-system breakpoints.
responsive.compact: Uses compact horizontal padding and full available width.
responsive.medium: Uses medium page padding and selected width policy.
responsive.wide: Uses standard page padding and selected maximum width.
responsive.ultrawide: Preserves maximum widths for reading and forms while allowing fluid data layouts.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Children must not create unexpected page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Horizontal padding must not consume excessive space at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: div or semantic element provided by the consumer
accessibility.accessibleName: Not required; meaningful child regions provide headings and landmarks.
aria: Do not add unnecessary landmark roles.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Not applicable to structural width behavior.

content.typical: Page header followed by several recipe regions.
content.maximum: Several route regions while retaining explicit spacing ownership.
content.localization: Width policies must tolerate expanded labels and text.
content.emptyBehavior: An empty PageContainer is normally invalid.

PageHeader.name: PageHeader
PageHeader.description: Canonical route-orientation header containing breadcrumbs, title, description, metadata, freshness, and a constrained action hierarchy.
capabilities: Identify the current route and primary user task.
Present supporting description and metadata.
Place one dominant page action and secondary utilities.
Transform action placement for compact layouts.

foundation.reason: Route orientation requires named slots, action hierarchy, responsive transformation, and shared spacing ownership.

compact.intent: Reduced route header for dense operational contexts.

slots.name: breadcrumbs
contentRestrictions: Do not repeat technical route structure.

slots.name: title
contentRestrictions: Exactly one route-level h1.

slots.name: description
contentRestrictions: Do not repeat obvious title wording.

slots.name: metadata
slots.description: Optional supporting scope, freshness, or context.
contentRestrictions: Do not place the complete page dataset here.

slots.name: actions
contentRestrictions: Normally one primary action.
Exports and low-frequency utilities remain secondary.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic density of the page header.
restrictions: Do not select compact only to reduce an incorrectly large title.

prohibitedParents: Card used only as an additional wrapper
spacingOwnership: PageHeader owns spacing between breadcrumbs, title, description, metadata, and actions.
The route recipe owns spacing between PageHeader and the next major region.
composition.surfaceOwnership: PageHeader normally renders directly on the page canvas.
rules: One PageHeader per ordinary route.
Do not repeat the same action elsewhere without a workflow reason.
Header height remains restrained in operational products.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Includes scope, freshness, and limited actions.
One collection-level primary action.
Does not duplicate form submission.
Sensitive actions remain outside the header.

notes: The screen supplies title, metadata, and actions.

responsive.strategy: Keep orientation first, stack actions when necessary, and move secondary utilities to overflow.
responsive.compact: Breadcrumbs may collapse; title, description, metadata, and primary action stack.
responsive.medium: Title group remains primary while actions wrap beside or below.
responsive.wide: Title group and actions align horizontally.
responsive.ultrawide: Header remains constrained and does not enlarge.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Secondary actions move to overflow before title or primary action becomes unreadable.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain readable and operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.accessibleName: The route-level h1 identifies the page.
keyboard: All actions and breadcrumbs are keyboard operable.
focus: Header content follows route and document order.
Route navigation may move focus to the h1 or main content according to application policy.
announcements: Freshness or critical context is announced by owning components.
aria: Do not apply banner role inside the application main content when it would duplicate the global header.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Action hierarchy and metadata meaning do not depend only on color.

content.typical: Breadcrumbs, title, concise description, metadata, one primary action, and secondary overflow.
content.maximum: A compact route orientation region; complex datasets belong below.
content.wrapping: Titles, descriptions, metadata, and actions wrap according to named slots.
content.truncation: Do not truncate the route title; lower-priority metadata may truncate with full-value access.
content.localization: Support expanded titles and actions without fixed heights.
content.emptyBehavior: A PageHeader without a title is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Raw route IDs, backend modules, DTO names, and UUIDs are prohibited unless explicitly user-relevant.

EntityHeader.name: EntityHeader
EntityHeader.description: Canonical compact orientation header for one entity, including identity, current status, essential metadata, freshness, and limited entity-level actions.
capabilities: Identify one domain entity.
Present current status and essential metadata.
Expose one entity-level primary action and secondary utilities.
Preserve entity orientation across detail sections.

foundation.reason: Entity orientation needs named slots, action constraints, responsive transformation, and reusable spacing ownership.

compact.intent: Reduced entity orientation inside a nested workspace.
prohibitedUse: Primary route orientation when critical metadata would be hidden.

slots.name: identity
slots.description: Entity title and optional user-facing secondary identifier.
contentRestrictions: Raw UUIDs remain secondary unless operationally required.

slots.name: status
contentRestrictions: Machine recommendation must not be represented as confirmed status.

slots.name: metadata
slots.description: Small collection of essential orientation metadata.
contentRestrictions: Do not include complete entity details.

slots.name: actions
contentRestrictions: One dominant entity-level action.
Destructive actions remain separated.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Compact variant must not remove essential orientation.

spacingOwnership: EntityHeader owns spacing among identity, status, metadata, and actions.
The entity-detail recipe owns spacing below the header.
composition.surfaceOwnership: EntityHeader may own one compact orientation surface.
rules: One primary EntityHeader per entity-detail route.
Do not repeat it inside every section.
Use domain components to map entity values into the slots.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Canonical implementation of entity orientation.
Use when one organization, user, or integration is being administered.
Review status must remain distinct from entity status.

notes: The entity or feature owner supplies mapped identity, status, metadata, and actions.

responsive.strategy: Stack identity, essential metadata, and actions before hiding secondary content.
responsive.compact: Identity, status, metadata, and primary action stack; secondary actions move to overflow.
responsive.medium: Identity and metadata remain primary; actions wrap.
responsive.ultrawide: Remains constrained and does not add low-value metadata.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Long identity values wrap; secondary metadata may truncate with full-value access.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain readable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: header containing the route-level entity h1
keyboard: All entity actions remain keyboard operable.
focus: Actions follow identity and metadata in logical order.
announcements: Material status changes are announced by the owning status component.
aria: Do not create a duplicate route-level heading.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Entity status and action hierarchy do not depend only on color.

content.typical: Identity, status, several essential metadata values, one primary action, and overflow utilities.
content.maximum: A compact orientation summary; complete details belong below.
content.wrapping: Identity and metadata wrap according to content contracts.
content.truncation: Primary identity remains accessible in full.
content.localization: Support long domain names and expanded status labels.
content.technicalContent: Raw UUIDs, database keys, transport states, and DTO names are prohibited unless explicitly operational.

Section.name: Section
Section.description: Canonical semantic content section with optional heading, description, actions, and controlled heading-to-content spacing.
capabilities: Create a meaningful document section.
Own spacing between section heading and content.
Place optional section-level actions.
Render without forcing a card surface.

foundation.reason: Native section semantics combined with shared spacing and action composition provide reusable structural hierarchy.

default.intent: Ordinary semantic content section without an independent surface.
prohibitedUse: Form field group without a section concept.

surface.intent: Section requiring a distinct interaction or content surface.

subtle.intent: Supporting or contextual section using a subdued surface.

slots.name: title
contentRestrictions: Heading level follows document hierarchy rather than visual size.

slots.name: description
contentRestrictions: Do not duplicate field-level help.

slots.name: actions
contentRestrictions: One dominant action at most.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Do not select surface merely to make the page look more designed.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Document heading level for the optional title.
restrictions: Must follow the screen heading hierarchy.

prohibitedChildren: Another Section used only to add padding
spacingOwnership: Section owns spacing between title, description, actions, and content.
The parent recipe owns spacing between sibling sections.
composition.surfaceOwnership: Section owns a surface only when the selected semantic variant requires it.
rules: Use Section for meaningful document structure.
Do not wrap every content fragment in a Section.
Do not use heading levels to obtain visual sizes.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Sections group metrics, analysis, and queues.
Active entity content uses semantic sections.
Sensitive actions require distinct semantic treatment.

responsive.strategy: Preserve document hierarchy while allowing heading actions to wrap below the title.
responsive.wide: Title group and actions may align horizontally.
responsive.ultrawide: Content remains governed by its parent width policy.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Content wraps or uses explicitly owned local overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Heading, description, actions, and content remain readable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: section when a meaningful accessible heading exists; otherwise a neutral container
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible section heading or explicit accessible label.
keyboard: Section itself has no keyboard interaction.
focus: Section does not alter document focus order.
aria: Do not add role=region to every visual group.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Surface hierarchy does not communicate critical meaning without textual context.

content.minimum: Meaningful content with an appropriate semantic relationship.
content.typical: Heading, concise description, optional action, and content body.
content.maximum: A coherent content region rather than an entire unrelated route.
content.wrapping: Heading, description, actions, and content wrap naturally.
content.emptyBehavior: A section with no content should not render unless it represents an explicit empty state.
content.technicalContent: Technical content is allowed only in explicitly approved audit or diagnostic sections.

Stack.name: Stack
Stack.description: Canonical one-dimensional layout utility that owns vertical or horizontal spacing between sibling elements.
capabilities: Apply consistent gap between sibling elements.
Arrange content vertically or horizontally.
Wrap horizontal groups when allowed.
Eliminate conflicting child margins.

foundation.source: CSS flex layout and spacing tokens
foundation.reason: Spacing ownership requires a constrained semantic alternative to repeated arbitrary flex and gap declarations.

horizontal.intent: Arrange sibling elements horizontally with controlled wrapping.

allowedUse: Screen-level region composition when the recipe permits it.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Sibling elements arranged by the stack.
contentRestrictions: Children must not add margins to recreate the same gap.

props.name: wrap
restrictions: Vertical stacks normally do not require wrap.

prohibitedChildren: Children using margins to duplicate the stack gap
spacingOwnership: Stack exclusively owns the gap between its direct children.
rules: Use one Stack when one-dimensional spacing is the actual relationship.
Do not nest stacks only to obtain arbitrary gaps.
Do not add child margins for the same sibling relationship.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for internal one-dimensional grouping.
FormSection and FormField may compose Stack internally.
Use to own subsection and panel gaps.

responsive.strategy: Preserve one-dimensional spacing while allowing approved direction or wrapping changes through parent composition.
responsive.compact: Horizontal stacks may wrap or become vertical when the owning component defines it.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Children determine content overflow; Stack must not force page-level overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Gap and wrapping remain usable at enlarged text sizes.

accessibility.semanticElement: div or semantic element supplied by the consumer
accessibility.accessibleName: Not required for purely structural use.
focus: Does not alter child focus order.
aria: Do not add unnecessary ARIA roles.

content.minimum: Two or more elements with a meaningful one-dimensional spacing relationship.
content.maximum: A manageable sibling group; complex spatial layouts require another component.
content.wrapping: Controlled by direction and wrap contract.
content.localization: Wrapping must support expanded child content.
content.emptyBehavior: An empty Stack normally should not render.

ContentGrid.name: ContentGrid
ContentGrid.description: Canonical responsive two-dimensional layout for content regions using approved column strategies, minimum widths, and token-backed gaps.
capabilities: Arrange peer content in responsive columns.
Collapse columns according to content requirements.
Apply consistent row and column gaps.
Prevent arbitrary screen-level grid definitions.

foundation.reason: Content grids require semantic column policies rather than repeated arbitrary grid utility combinations.

autoFit.intent: Create as many readable columns as fit within an approved minimum item width.

balanced.intent: Use a constrained fixed column count that collapses predictably.

dominant.intent: Provide one dominant content column and one supporting column.
allowedUse: Dashboard main chart and secondary panel.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Peer or intentionally weighted grid items.
contentRestrictions: Items must follow the selected grid semantic relationship.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Do not select solely to achieve a desired column count.

prohibitedChildren: Children using absolute positioning for ordinary alignment
spacingOwnership: ContentGrid owns row and column gaps between direct children.
rules: Items must remain readable at their minimum width.
Do not use a universal equal card grid for unrelated content priorities.
Use SplitPane when panels have asymmetric scroll or resize behavior.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Metrics and analytical panels use different grid policies.
Use only when peer or dominant/supporting relationships are clear.
Forms remain constrained and should not be forced into arbitrary grids.

responsive.strategy: Collapse columns according to minimum readable item widths and semantic priority.
responsive.medium: One or two columns according to item complexity.
responsive.ultrawide: Adds columns only when item readability and hierarchy remain valid.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Grid items must shrink safely or stack; page-level horizontal overflow is prohibited.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Columns collapse before text or controls become unreadable.

accessibility.semanticElement: div or semantic parent supplied by the consumer
accessibility.accessibleName: Not required for purely structural use.
focus: DOM order must remain logical across visual column changes.
aria: Do not use grid role unless implementing an interactive ARIA grid.

content.minimum: Two peer or intentionally weighted items.
content.typical: Several metric, panel, or summary components.
content.maximum: A bounded region collection; large server collections require DataTable or list patterns.
content.wrapping: Items stack according to the selected layout strategy.
content.localization: Column collapse must tolerate localized expansion.
content.emptyBehavior: An empty ContentGrid should not render.

SplitPane.name: SplitPane
SplitPane.description: Canonical asymmetric multi-panel workspace for master-detail, evidence-review, comparison, or contextual-side-panel layouts with explicit scroll and responsive ownership.
capabilities: Arrange primary and secondary panels asymmetrically.
Assign panel width and scroll ownership.
Transform secondary panels into stacked content or overlays.
Preserve the primary task when horizontal space decreases.

foundation.source: CSS Grid, layout recipes, and optional resizable-panel foundation
foundation.reason: Multi-panel workspaces require explicit panel roles, scroll ownership, width constraints, and compact transformation.

primaryAside.intent: One flexible primary panel and one constrained supporting aside.

masterDetail.intent: Persistent selection list and flexible selected-item detail.

review.intent: Evidence navigation, authoritative source, and constrained proposal or recommendation panel.

comparison.intent: Present two peer states or versions for direct comparison.

slots.name: navigation
slots.description: Optional master list or evidence navigator.
contentRestrictions: Must have an accessible label.
Independent scroll requires explicit ownership.

slots.name: primary
slots.description: Main task or authoritative content panel.
contentRestrictions: Primary panel retains the greatest usable width.

slots.name: secondary
slots.description: Supporting context, proposal, or details panel.
contentRestrictions: Critical information must not exist only in a collapsible secondary panel.

props.name: variant
restrictions: Select according to the layout recipe and dominant task.

props.name: secondaryCollapsible
props.description: Allows the secondary panel to collapse when the workflow supports progressive disclosure.
restrictions: Critical content must not be hidden by default.

spacingOwnership: SplitPane owns gaps and dividers between direct panels.
Each panel owns its internal content spacing.
composition.surfaceOwnership: SplitPane does not require one outer surface; individual panels own surfaces according to their roles.
rules: The primary panel retains task priority.
Scroll ownership is explicit per panel.
Compact transformation must be defined before implementation.
Do not use SplitPane solely to create visual variety.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Contextual aside moves below the primary content on medium layouts.
Preview remains optional and must not compress comparison columns.
Canonical wide-layout review workspace.
Administration navigation remains constrained.

notes: Panel selection and visibility are supplied by the owning screen or feature.
Shareable selected entities may be URL-owned outside SplitPane.
Responsive overlay transformation requires focus management.
Independent panel scrolling must be explicit.

responsive.strategy: Remove persistent secondary panels before compressing the primary task below usable width.
responsive.compact: Panels become sequential content or navigation and secondary drawers.
responsive.medium: Navigation or secondary panel moves to a drawer or below primary content.
responsive.wide: Persistent split panels according to the selected semantic variant.
responsive.ultrawide: Panel widths remain constrained; primary content gains additional space.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Independent panel scrolling is allowed only when declared and tested; page-level horizontal overflow is prohibited.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Panels must stack or collapse before content becomes unusable at 125% browser zoom.

accessibility.semanticElement: structural container with labeled nav, main section, and optional aside
accessibility.accessibleName: Each semantic panel has a visible heading or accessible label.
keyboard: Independent scroll regions are reachable and escapable by keyboard.
focus: DOM order follows navigation, primary, and secondary reading order.
Visual reordering must not create illogical focus order.
announcements: Selected master item or evidence changes update orientation when necessary.
Collapsed and expanded state is exposed.
aria: Do not use ARIA grid for ordinary layout.
Label independent navigation and aside regions.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Selected panel item, active evidence, and differences must not depend only on color.

content.minimum: One primary panel and one meaningful panel relationship.
content.typical: Navigation or primary content with one supporting panel.
content.maximum: Three controlled panels in a review workflow.
content.wrapping: Panel content wraps or uses explicitly owned internal overflow.
content.truncation: Primary decision content must remain accessible in full.
content.localization: Panel minimum widths and collapse points tolerate expanded text.
content.emptyBehavior: Missing secondary content removes or replaces the secondary panel without reserving blank space.
content.technicalContent: Technical content is allowed only in explicitly approved diagnostic or audit panels.

checks.description: The layout component catalog must validate against the component catalog schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing layout catalog fields.

checks.description: Layout components must not duplicate canonical ownership or public import paths.
Shared layout components must not import feature, entity, route, query, permission, or transport modules.
checks.remediation: Move domain and data behavior to the owning entity, feature, or route.

checks.description: Layout components must not introduce unexpected page-level horizontal overflow at approved viewports and zoom levels.
checks.remediation: Correct width, wrapping, panel transformation, or scroll ownership.

checks.description: Every structural gap, surface, scroll container, and responsive transformation must have one explicit owner.
checks.remediation: Correct component contracts or selected layout composition.

checks.description: Page-local flex, grid, container, and header patterns similar to canonical layout components require review.
checks.remediation: Reuse the canonical layout component or document why the local pattern remains distinct.
